newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia has no problems with democracy -Pangalos.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia has no problems with democracy -Pangalos.

text.p: Slovak democracy is healthy and Greece will support its application for membership of NATO, the EU and the OECD, Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos said on Tuesday.
"We will do everything to support Slovakia's OECD membership," Pangalos told a news conference after meeting Slovak Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik.
"The only criteria for membership should be economic performance and our impression of Slovakia's is very positive," he added.
"Economic performance should also be the only criterion for EU membership...Slovakia has no problems with democracy and we don't think there is anything wrong with Slovakia," Pangalos said.
The Greek minister's statements came as balm to a beleagured Hamzik, who has become the lightening rod for western criticism of Slovakia.
Slovakia has come under fire from the EU, NATO member countries and the United States, all of whom have expressed concern over Slovakia's foot-dragging on the path towards democracy.
They have also said that lack of progress in questions of democracy and human rights could impair Slovakia's chances of being among the first wave of new members of the EU and NATO.
Slovakia, once mentioned with the Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary as a prime candidate for NATO membership, has now largely dropped out of official mention in the west.
It is to hold a referendum on NATO membership at the end of May.

"We are for the inclusion in NATO of those countries whose population has stated itself in favour of membership," Pangalos said. "We hope the referendum on this subject will be positive and are convinced Slovak (NATO) participation will enhance security in Europe."
Pangalos arrived in Bratislava on Monday and left on Tuesday.
